newsitem.title: USA: U.S. offers farm credits to Brazil, others.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers farm credits to Brazil, others.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday it was offering Brazil $150 million in farm export credit guarantees under the GSM-102 program for fiscal 1997.
It also offered $80 million to East Caribbean countries, and $40 million to the West Caribbean, and made smaller allocations for Tunisia, India, Croatia and Lithuania.

Of Brazil's $150 million, USDA allocated $75 million to wheat, cotton, rice, feed grains, breeder livestock, poultry breeder stock, poultry breeder stock, fresh fruit, hops, tallow, meat, peanuts and other commodities.
No specific dollar allocation was made for individual commodities, to give buyers and sellers maximum flexibility, USDA said. The remaining $75 million was unallocated.
USDA offered $20 million to Tunisia under the same program, $15 million to India, $12 million to Croatia, and $1.5 million to Lithuania.
